Heard learned counsel for the petitioner as well as Sri Gyan Prakash, learned Senior Advocate/Deputy Solicitor General of India, assisted by Sri Sanjay Kumar Yadav, for the Central Bureau of Investigation (for short ?CBI?) and perused the record.

2. The present petition under Article 227 of the Constitution of India has been filed for setting aside the judgement and order dated 21.1.2021 passed by the Special Judge (P.C. Act) CBI/Additional Sessions Judge, Court No.2, Ghaziabad as well as the cognizance order dated 8.1.2020 passed by the Special Judicial Magistrate, CBI, Ghaziabad and the entire proceedings of Case No.7 of 2020 (CBI Vs. Bhikhari Singh and others), arising out of charge sheet in Crime NoRC1202015A0008 dated 31.12.2019, under Sections 120-B, 420, 409, 201 IPC, Police Station CBI/ACB, District Ghaziabad,
pending in the court of Special Judicial Magistrate, CBI, Ghaziabad.

1 3.

Under the direction of this Court vide order dated 30.1.2014 passed in Writ Petition No.12802 (MB) of 2011 for misappropriation of MNREGA funds in seven districts of the State of Uttar Pradesh, namely, Balrampur, Gonda, Mahoba, Sonebhadra, Sant Kabir Nagar, Mirzapur and Kushinagar between 2007 to 2010, the investigation was transferred to the CBI.
4. After investigating the offence, charge sheet has been filed.
The CBI in its investigation has found the involvement and role played by the petitioner in commission of the offence.
The CBI in its investigation report has clearly said that the facts and the evidence were available against the petitioner for his involvement in commission of offence.

The revisional court vide impugned order,
has dismissed the revision on the ground that the learned trial court has not committed any error of law or jurisdiction while taking cognizance on the charge sheet and summoning the petitioner to face the trial.
5. The scope for interference of this Court in exercise of its jurisdiction under Article 227 of the Constitution of India is limited.
Once the material and evidence disclosed the commission of offence, this Court would not interfere with the order of cognizance or criminal proceedings against the petitioner.

This Court finds that the courts below have not committed any error of law or jurisdiction, which requires interference by this Court in exercise of its jurisdiction under Article 227 of the Constitution of India.
6. Thus, the petition being devoid of merit and substance, is dismissed.

7. However, it is provided that the petitioner may take all peas at the time of framing of charge that no offence is made out against him from the material and evidence collected during the course of investigation.
The trial court shall deal with the said pleas of the petitioner at the time of framing of charge and then will proceed to pass an appropriate order.

Order Date :- 21.2.2023 Rao/-
